findings.title: basedOn.g09v3.role calls in-host-process 'a third mode', contradicting the same sentence's own '2 modes' and misdescribing the live v9 census, in which in-host-process is one of exactly two modes
findings.theSentence: '28-cell census is 2 platforms x 7 tokens x 2 modes; architecture axis STATED INVARIANT. This catalog does not re-author that census and does not admit a third in-host-process mode.'
findings.measuredAgainstLive: Live v9 truthTables.executionModes.modes has exactly TWO keys: child-process and in-host-process. The census method reads 'cells = platforms x tokens x execution modes = 2 x 7 x 2', and byPlatformAndMode enumerates only child-process/ and in-host-process/ prefixes. v9 elsewhere calls it 'this artifact's two-mode split', and ID-DEP-P10 is stated as 'which component execution modes V2 admits -- host-spawned child process, in-host-process, or both'. There are two candidate modes and in-host-process is the second of them. There is no reading under which it is a third.
findings.whyItIsNotMerelyCosmetic: It is self-contradictory inside one sentence: the first clause states 2 modes and the second calls one of those two a third. It also concerns precisely the mode this fixture class exists to discuss, and that mode carries 14 of the 28 census cells — 7 per platform, all DISCLOSURE-ONLY. A reader who took 'third' at face value would model the census as gaining a new axis on admission, when v9's own intent says the corpus 'runs again in that mode', an already-tabulated one.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: The operative clause is TRUE — the catalog does not admit the mode — and that non-admission is stated correctly in five other places without the word 'third': authorityClaim, purpose, whatIsNotAuthored, the state's inHostProcessMode NOT-ADMITTED, and doesNot. The rest of the same role sentence is also true: the census is 28 cells, 2 platforms, 7 tokens, 2 modes, and live G09 v3 does carry 'STATED INVARIANT across the two architectures'. G09 v3 uses the word 'third' zero times, so the error is the subject's own and not a quotation.
findings.notIntroducedByTheRepair: The g09v3 role is byte-identical in v1 and v2. This is a defect carried forward untouched, not one the restoration created. It is raised here because v1 was never reviewed, so this is the first opportunity to raise it.
findings.howItGradesAgainstThePrecedingVerdicts: Against FC-RO, which stayed an OBSERVATION: there the defect was an omission in a secondary field while the primary quotation was exact and the dropped material survived elsewhere. Two of those three mitigations apply here — the location is secondary and fx10Intent is exact — but the first does not, because this is an ASSERTION THAT IS FALSE rather than an omission, and in the FX-6 v1 verdict I recorded that a truncation under-informs while an altered or false statement misinforms. Against FX-5 v1 and FX-6 v1, which were SHOULD-FIX: those were false or altered in the source-of-record field, which is worse than here. This lands as SHOULD-FIX on the checkable-and-false test rather than on location.
findings.propagationRisk: This family cites each other's role annotations by design — FX-7 v2 cited FX-5 v2's convention, FX-8 v2 cited FX-2B's posture. A wrong mode count in a role is exactly the shape that propagates; this reviewer watched the 'last Claude ACCEPT 0/0' formulation propagate across five doctor corpora earlier in this session before it was corrected.
findings.fix: One word. Delete 'third', or write 'does not admit the in-host-process mode'. No authored state changes and no other clause needs touching.

decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record as-is. The repair this v2 exists to perform is complete and correct and should be kept verbatim: fx10Intent == live at 382 of 382, fx10Proves == live, the predecessor claim is exact, the diff is surgical, and every dispatch prohibition is respected — the mode is not admitted in any of five places, no census-run bytes exist, and the bare-integer set is only census facts carried from v9. A v3 that deletes the single word 'third' from basedOn.g09v3.role, or rewrites that clause as 'does not admit the in-host-process mode', would on these bytes carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer. It could also name CLAUDE-FX10-SF1 in lands, which is now available where it was not before.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: The repair landed perfectly and the finding is elsewhere, so take those separately. fx10Intent == live v9 at 382 characters against 382, restoring the sentence v1 had dropped — 'A run in that mode that reports any cell as enforced is a defect in the test, the mode, or the table' — and fx10Proves is present and == equal to live where v1 had none. The predecessor claim '280-of-382 true prefix' is exact on every element, measured against v1's own bytes because no reviewer has ever verified v1. The diff is surgical: zero paths removed, five added, six changed of which four are identity or prose, and every initialStates path byte-identical. Every dispatch prohibition holds — I read all eight in-host-process mentions in context and five are explicit non-admissions, censusRun is NOT-AUTHORED, 'ENFORCED' occurs once inside a not-authored line, and the bare integers are only 0, 2, 26 and 7, all census facts carried from v9. The finding is in a role annotation. basedOn.g09v3.role says '28-cell census is 2 platforms x 7 tokens x 2 modes ... and does not admit a third in-host-process mode.' That sentence contradicts itself: it states 2 modes and then calls one of those two a third. I checked the mode count in two independent places rather than trusting the census summary — live v9 truthTables.executionModes.modes has exactly two keys, child-process and in-host-process, and ID-DEP-P10 frames the open question as 'which component execution modes V2 admits -- host-spawned child process, in-host-process, or both'. v9 also calls it 'this artifact's two-mode split'. There is no reading under which in-host-process is a third mode, and G09 v3 itself uses the word 'third' zero times, so this is the subject's own error and not a quotation. Four of that role's five claims verify; only this one is false. It crosses to SHOULD-FIX rather than staying an observation because it is an ASSERTION that is false rather than an omission — the distinction I drew in the FX-6 v1 verdict, where a truncation under-informs but a false statement misinforms — and because it concerns precisely the mode this class exists to discuss, one that carries 14 of the 28 census cells. Two things make it milder and I want them on the record. First, the operative clause is true: the catalog does not admit the mode, and that non-admission is stated correctly five other times without the word. Second, the role is BYTE-IDENTICAL in v1 and v2, so this is a carried-forward defect the restoration never touched, not one it introduced — it surfaces now only because FX-10 v1 was never reviewed, which is the third chain in a row with that shape after FX-7 and FX-8. That is worth your attention on its own: if other unreviewed v1s were superseded the same way, their v2s may be carrying similar untouched annotations. Custody is otherwise clean: subject unmoved at a5c51108 and 0444 at both samplings, v1 unmoved at 09bf8aa6, five of five cited digests equal live bytes, G09 v3 confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict, the D-163 join confirms OBL-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with FX-10 inside its fourteen, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, no control bytes, SATISFIED and QUALIFIED at zero.
